body.text:
Here's where things stood, and what I did about it.

## Where the project was

Last commit was `2c37dc6` (GPU embeddings — a Tier-0 detour that fixed reindex: 30 min → 78s). The desktop work per [DESKTOP.md](architecture/DESKTOP.md) §5 had step 1 (squash-merge fold) and step 4a (the Electron shell) done, but **steps 2 and 3 were untouched** — the read-only API groundwork and the branch/diff UI the shell was supposed to grow into. Baseline was green (build + all tests) before I touched anything.

## What I built (steps 2 + 3, committed as `d487e6a`)

**Server** — new [reviewGit.ts](packages/cli/src/commands/reviewGit.ts), plus wiring in review.ts:
- `GET /api/branches` — local branches, current one marked, upstream ahead/behind. Reads `refs/heads/` only, so our metadata refs can't leak into a branch list structurally rather than by filtering.
- `GET /api/diff/:sha` — per-file diff parsed into hunks and numbered lines; rename/copy/binary/mode detection.
- `GET /api/overview?rev=` and `git for-ai report --rev` (that walk was missing on the CLI too).
- `/api/meta` gained `capabilities`, so one SPA build serves browser and desktop by asking the server, not sniffing the client.

**UI** — branch chips that scope the timeline (state in the URL), and a diff pane rendered beneath each change's recorded intent.

Three judgment calls worth your eye, all in the file headers:
- **Merge commits diff against the first parent, with a warning saying so.** `git show` on a merge prints nothing, which would render as "this merge changed nothing".
- **Truncation clips bodies, never counts** — past the render budget the +/− tallies keep going while lines stop being stored.
- **Deviation from the spec, recorded not silent:** DESKTOP.md said branch *sidebar*; I shipped a chip row. This page is one narrow reading column and most repos have a handful of branches. The component's contract (rev in, rev out) is sidebar-ready if the desktop window grows panes. **Syntax highlighting is deferred** — the one piece of §3 item 3 I didn't build; no bundled highlighter earns its weight yet.

## Verification

632 tests green (up from ~570), gating build and test run unpiped. Also ran the real server against this repo and read the pages in a browser: branch bar, a real diff, and the truncation warning firing on a genuinely large commit. Server process stopped afterwards.

## Next

DESKTOP.md step 4b — the token-gated POST action endpoints (`sync`/`reindex`/`annotate`/`relink`/`init`) and the actions panel. That's the last functional piece before packaging, and it's the first place the desktop app stops being read-only, so the per-launch token design deserves care. Say the word and I'll start there.

git commit -F - <<'MSG'
The page opens in under a second, and stops talking about itself

Two owner-reported problems with the review UI, both fixed.

1. "Hangs on Reading the repository…" — it wasn't hanging, it was
taking 123 SECONDS on this 41-commit repo. Not one slow git command:
thousands of git PROCESSES. Every commit's identity lookup called
findEntryByCommitSha, which re-reads the ENTIRE change-map with one
`cat-file` per change; notes and sessions were read one spawn at a
time too. At ~25-30ms per spawn on Windows that is the whole two
minutes. Now ~1.2s for the same walk (~100x), and /api/overview
answers in 0.66s.

The fix is batching, not a new git strategy (ARCHITECTURE §4.1
predicted exactly this and prescribed exactly this):
- core: catFileBatch reads N objects in ONE `git cat-file --batch`.
  It frames objects by BYTE length, which is the subtle part - this
  repo's own ledger is full of em-dashes, and a character-indexed
  parser corrupts every object after the first multi-byte one. Tested
  directly.
- core: readChangeMapSnapshot - the whole map, read once, queried in
  memory (entryForCommit / entryForChangeId / surviving). Two git
  invocations instead of two per commit.
- core: readLedgerNotesForCommits (notes list + one batch read) and
  readSessionRecords (same shape for the sessions ref).
- report.ts uses all three: one snapshot + two note batches + one
  session batch per run. The rare trailer-recovery path still calls
  resolveChangeId (it WRITES, healing identity) and re-reads the
  snapshot afterwards, so semantics are unchanged, including the
  non-minting read guarantee.
- /api/overview now defaults to the most recent 300 commits; a page
  must open promptly on a 50,000-commit repo. `git for-ai report`
  still walks all of history - it is making a document, not painting
  a screen.

New tests assert EQUIVALENCE, not speed (a wall-clock threshold on a
shared machine is a flaky test): every bulk reader returns exactly
what the single-item reader it replaces returns, on real repos -
including missing objects, malformed notes, folded changes, and the
multi-byte framing hazard.

2. The UI read like our changelog, not a product. Owner: "i do not
care about your journey to get to this... why put them on the screen
lol." Gone from the screen: the footer explaining that a read-only
server on 127.0.0.1 serves the page and that agents use --json
instead; "never inferred or fabricated"; ledger / change-map / spans /
"captured intent" / "synthesis" / "the local index". In their place,
plain product language: "no reasoning recorded", "session recording
on", "Merge commit - showing what it brought in", "Very large commit -
some file diffs are shortened."

What did NOT change is the honesty itself: every missing-data state is
still labeled and still true. Only the essay defending it is gone.
Recorded as CLAUDE.md hard rule 10 so it doesn't creep back, with the
batching rule as 11.

Also fixed in passing: the ask panel told users to run `git for-ai
index`, which is not a command (it's `reindex`).

Copy pass delegated to a background Sonnet agent (scoped to
review-ui's visible strings); its diff reviewed line by line here,
server-side strings and the cross-cutting vocabulary done in this
session. Tests: 645 green (core 268 incl. 11 new, cli 233, review-ui
60, schemas 66, desktop 18). Verified live against this repo: page
loads instantly, new copy renders, diff warnings read plainly.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
